title: Choose Bon Laundry’s new visual world
question: Each direction keeps the real workflows intact; it changes only how the system helps customers and operators read live laundry operations.

options.label: Hydro Dispatch Desk
options.thesis: A composed service desk where live machine capacity is the first thing every role can understand.
options.viewport: A live service pulse, a concise workload strip, and role-specific actions in one calm operating frame.
options.risk: Requires disciplined content restraint so dense operations do not become too quiet.

raised.raise: Color is reserved for state changes; the working field remains calm and highly legible.
A strict visible alignment system keeps dense data operational instead of card-led.

options.label: Service Ledger
options.thesis: A warm, editorial workspace that makes booking and machine care feel considered rather than technical.
options.viewport: A clear daily ledger with a live fleet strip and immediate next action for every role.
options.risk: Its familiar premium-dashboard rhythm is less distinctive than the live-board directions.

options.label: Live Service Board
options.lineage: a premium transit board paired with a service pass
options.thesis: Laundry moves through the shop as an explicit journey: check in, allocate, run, collect.
options.viewport: Customers see their service pass; staff see a ranked live board; managers see the same flow as fleet capacity.
options.case: Wins on audience identification and product clarity: the queue and machine assignment are genuinely time-based journeys.
options.risk: Must stay unmistakably laundry-specific, not imitate an airline interface.

options.label: Measured Grid
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel’s precise typographic construction grid
options.thesis: A rigorously aligned field where machine capacity and queue timing become an elegant operational map.
options.viewport: A striking grid-led overview with live machine cells and a single focused action panel.
options.case: Holds clarity but gives customers less immediate narrative than the live-service journey.
options.risk: Can feel more like an analytics poster than a welcoming service experience.

options.label: Cycle Studio
options.thesis: Every order has a visible progression through wash, dry, fold, and collection.
options.viewport: The laundry cycle is a single, human-readable sequence with current state held in view.
options.case: Holds customer understanding but loses operational speed in busy POS and queue screens.
options.risk: A darker, more atmospheric field may feel too slow for front-counter work.

options.label: Iridescent Calm
options.lineage: a cloud edge with restrained spectral state bands
options.thesis: Quiet white space with color appearing only when capacity or attention changes.
options.viewport: A nearly white command field with rare, beautiful state transitions.
options.case: Declined: it loses both operating speed and brand specificity.

options.label: One-bit Console
options.thesis: A high-contrast, windowed utility console for machine and queue actions.
options.viewport: Operational windows tile over a single desktop surface.
options.case: Declined: it compromises the approachable, fresh brand promise.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS dashboard executed to a high production bar.
canonCard.viewport: The familiar dashboard arrangement users already know.
